what: Share the Power. Earn $1,000*. You already made a smart move taking control of your energy. Now pass that power on to a neighbor, friend, or family member — and get paid $1,000 for doing it.
reward: Share the Power. Earn $1,000*. You already made a smart move taking control of your energy. Now pass that power on to a neighbor, friend, or family member — and get paid $1,000 for doing it.
requirements: Referrers participate via Sunrun's referral program (customer referral page addresses existing Sunrun customers; a separate non-customer program exists with its own guidelines). Referee must be a new customer who signs a Sunrun Customer Agreement, receives Sunrun Sign Off within one year of the referral, and pays applicable upfront/deposit fees; both accounts in good standing.
payout_timing: No expiry on the current offer; the reward is paid within ~90 days after installation begins on the referee's system (months after the referral is made).
payout_value_note: flat $1,000 per qualifying referral (official headline offer); paid via reward card, not cash
catches: Payment is contingent on a completed conversion: the referee must sign a Sunrun Customer Agreement, receive Sunrun Sign Off within one year of the referral, and pay any upfront/deposit fees — referrals that don't convert earn $0.

The $1,000 Referral Reward is issued in a form determined by Sunrun — typically a prepaid or gift reward card (Visa) that is non-transferable, not for resale, not redeemable for cash, and expires six months after issuance.
Both your and the referee's Sunrun accounts must be paid in full and in good standing at the time of payment.
Reward arrives within 90 days of installation beginning on the referee's system (per the general terms) — this is a months-long wait, not instant.
Cannot refer someone in the same household (second-home exception only); first to submit wins if multiple people refer the same person.
Rewards may be taxable — Sunrun may require tax documentation to issue a 1099; participants are responsible for reporting the reward.
Sunrun reserves the right to suspend or cancel promotions without notice.

This route covers the customer referral program (the referral page speaks to existing customers: 'You already made a smart move taking control of your energy'); non-customer referral amounts are set by separate program guidelines.
Standard disclosure: this is a referral-sharing route — share only with people who have consented to be contacted, per Sunrun's terms and telemarketing rules.

steps.text: Get your personal Sunrun referral link (from your Sunrun account or the referral page).
Share the link with a neighbor, friend, or family member who is considering solar and has consented to be contacted.
Your referee signs a Sunrun Customer Agreement, receives Sunrun Sign Off within one year of the referral, and pays any upfront/deposit fees.

The $1,000 Referral Reward (typically a prepaid/gift reward card) is issued within 90 days of installation beginning on the referee's system, provided both accounts are paid in full and in good standing.
steps.done_when: The reward has arrived for both of you.

what: Indiana taxpayers are eligible for a state income tax credit of 20% of contributions to an Indiana529 Direct Savings Plan account, up to $1,500 credit per year ($750 for married couples filing separately).
reward: Indiana taxpayers are eligible for a state income tax credit of 20% of contributions to an Indiana529 Direct Savings Plan account, up to $1,500 credit per year ($750 for married couples filing separately).
requirements: Indiana taxpayer (resident or non-resident, individual or married) who contributes to an Indiana529 account.
payout_timing: Annual cycle: contribute during the calendar tax year, then claim the credit when filing that year's Indiana income tax return.
payout_value_note: 20% of contributions (up to $7,500/yr) = max $1,500/yr credit; nonrefundable Indiana tax credit, not cash.
catches: A nonrefundable state tax credit, not cash: it only saves money if you owe Indiana income tax; contribute $0 or owe $0 in Indiana tax and you get $0.
Must be an Indiana taxpayer (resident or non-resident) contributing to an Indiana529 account.

The credit may be recaptured from the account owner for rollovers to another state's 529 plan, federal non-qualified withdrawals, out-of-Indiana K-12 tuition withdrawals, education loan repayments, or Roth IRA rollovers.
Non-qualified withdrawals: earnings face federal income tax plus a 10% federal penalty tax, plus state and local income taxes - consult a tax professional.
The official footnote ties the stated credit terms to the Indiana529 Direct Savings Plan; confirm advisor-sold or CD plan treatment in the Disclosure Booklet.

steps.text: Open an Indiana529 account online (minimum $10 to start).
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Contribute to the account during the calendar tax year.
Claim the 20% credit on your Indiana state income tax return (up to $1,500 per year; $750 if married filing separately).
Keep the funds for qualified education expenses to avoid credit recapture.

what: Approved recipients can receive matching scholarships of tuition units worth up to $2,000 at today's prices, while top-scoring recipients also can receive a one-time grant of tuition units worth $3,000 at today's prices.
reward: Approved recipients can receive matching scholarships of tuition units worth up to $2,000 at today's prices, while top-scoring recipients also can receive a one-time grant of tuition units worth $3,000 at today's prices.
requirements: Texas resident student in grades 3-9 who is a Texas Tuition Promise Fund beneficiary and the tax dependent of a Texas resident, with family income of $120,000 or less.
payout_timing: Annual cycle: applications September 1-December 31; approvals notified in April; minimum contributions due by August 31; scholarship units deposited by end of September.
payout_value_note: Tuition units, not cash; up to $2,000 match; top scorers may also get a one-time $3,000 tuition-unit grant.
catches: Competitive, not guaranteed: applications are scored on grade averages, income levels, and number of dependents; only approved recipients receive awards.
Grades 3-9 only; Texas resident; family income $120,000 or less; the child must be a Texas Tuition Promise Fund (prepaid tuition plan) beneficiary.
Awards are tuition units, not cash - deposited to a Foundation-owned scholarship account and disbursed directly to Texas public colleges for undergraduate resident tuition and required fees only.
At least $50 in Promise Fund contributions during the sales period (September 1-August 31) is required to receive an award.
Must reapply each year; the Promise (tuition grant) scholarship can be received only once.
Non-qualified use of 529 funds carries federal income tax on earnings plus a 10% federal penalty - consult a tax advisor.

steps.text: Confirm the child's eligibility (Texas Tuition Promise Fund beneficiary, grades 3-9, Texas resident, family income $120,000 or less).
Read the Matching Scholarship and Tuition Grant Description and Application Instructions.
Have the child research a career and write the student career essay; obtain the prior school year's report card or transcript.
steps.done_when: You've got the Prior School Year.

steps.text: Apply online at MatchThePromise.org (or by mail) between September 1 and December 31.
If approved, submit the federal tax return for income verification by May 31 and ensure at least $50 in contributions to the Promise Fund contract during the sales period (Sept 1-Aug 31).

what: For every dollar you deposit to the TNStars account by June 30 of the qualifying period, the State will match it with $4 - up to $500 per child, per year, with a lifetime maximum match of $1,500.
reward: For every dollar you deposit to the TNStars account by June 30 of the qualifying period, the State will match it with $4 - up to $500 per child, per year, with a lifetime maximum match of $1,500.
requirements: Tennessee resident applicant with a child age 14 or younger meeting TIPS household income requirements.
payout_timing: Current qualifying period: applications and qualifying deposits through June 30, 2026; match on deposits made August 1-June 30 of the qualifying period.
payout_value_note: 4-to-1 on own deposits; $25 min deposit earns $100; $500/yr and $1,500 lifetime max per child.
catches: Tennessee residents only; the child must be 14 or younger; household income limits apply (reference-guide example: a family of 4 earning under $80,375 can qualify).
4-to-1 on YOUR deposits: deposit $25, get $100; deposit $125, get the $500 yearly max; deposit $0, get $0.
Applications and qualifying deposits for the current period close June 30, 2026.
$500 per child per year and a $1,500 lifetime maximum match per child.
Standard 529 risk: non-qualified withdrawals face federal income tax on earnings plus a 10% federal penalty - consult a tax advisor.

steps.text: Check eligibility at Treasury.TN.gov/TIPS (Tennessee resident, child 14 or younger, household income limits).
Complete the TIPS Program Application during the qualifying period (applications accepted through June 30, 2026).
Once approved, open a TNStars account for each child (as little as $25 to start).
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Deposit to the TNStars account by June 30 of the qualifying period; the state matches $4 for every $1 deposited.

what: The State of New Jersey is offering a one-time matching grant of up to $750 for initial deposits into a new NJBEST 529 College Savings Plan. This dollar-for-dollar grant will match the first contribution made by New Jersey residents who open an NJBEST account for a new student beneficiary.
reward: The State of New Jersey is offering a one-time matching grant of up to $750 for initial deposits into a new NJBEST 529 College Savings Plan. This dollar-for-dollar grant will match the first contribution made by New Jersey residents who open an NJBEST account for a new student beneficiary.
requirements: New Jersey resident NJBEST (or Franklin Templeton) 529 account owner with household AGI $0-$75,000 opening an account for a new student beneficiary.
payout_timing: One-time grant: apply within one year of funding the account; maintain the contribution for three years.
payout_value_note: Dollar-for-dollar of initial deposit; $25 minimum to open.
catches: Account owner must be a New Jersey resident with household AGI between $0 and $75,000.
Dollar-for-dollar on the initial deposit only: deposit $25, get $25; deposit $750 or more, get $750; limited to one grant per beneficiary.
The grant application must be submitted within one year of funding the account.
Keep up to $750 of the initial contribution in the account for a minimum of three years or the matching grant is forfeited back to HESAA.
Program is subject to available funding.
Non-qualified withdrawals face federal income tax on earnings plus a 10% federal penalty - consult a tax advisor.

steps.text: Open a new NJBEST 529 account (as little as $25) for a new student beneficiary.
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Make the initial deposit (matched dollar-for-dollar up to $750).
Submit the NJBEST Matching Grant application within one year of funding, attaching prior-year IRS tax return transcripts (or documented proof of income).
Keep the account open and maintain up to $750 of the initial contribution for at least three years.
steps.done_when: The account stays open and in good standing.

what: Reward Card: $100 reward card for existing customer per referral. $100 reward card for new customer. Lifetime maximum of 10 referral reward cards per customer.
reward: Reward Card: $100 reward card for existing customer per referral. $100 reward card for new customer. Lifetime maximum of 10 referral reward cards per customer.
requirements: Existing AT&T wireless or FirstNet Subscriber Paid customers referring new customers; new customer must be eligible & verified for FirstNet (public-safety employee/volunteer), complete verification within 30 days, and open a new line on an eligible FirstNet unlimited plan (min $54/month).
payout_timing: No expiry on the current flyer (subject to change); reward notification within 60 days of eligible activation, redemption within 75 days of notification, card delivered 3–4 weeks after redemption.
payout_value_note: flat $100 reward card per qualifying referral to the existing customer; $1,000 lifetime cap (10 referrals) in catches only
catches: FirstNet-only: eligibility is limited to eligible & verified employees/volunteers of qualifying public safety entities (or supporting entities); the new customer must qualify for FirstNet service and complete verification within 30 days.
The new customer must open a NEW line on an eligible FirstNet unlimited voice-and-data plan (minimum $54/month) — upgrades are not eligible; tablets, wearables, and hotspots are excluded.
The new line must remain active with the qualifying plan for a minimum of 30 days from activation or no reward is issued.

Reward card (not cash): the AT&T Visa Reward Card has no cash access, expires 6 months after issuance (month-end), and must be redeemed within 75 days of the reward notification — miss the redemption window and it's gone.
Redemption and delivery take time: notification within 60 days of eligible activation, then the card is delivered 3–4 weeks after redemption.
Lifetime maximum of 10 referral reward cards per customer — the lifetime cap belongs in catches, per lane rules (10 x $100 = $1,000 lifetime).
Offer 'subject to change and may be discontinued at any time.'
Excludes FirstNet Agency Paid users and migrations from Cricket, GoPhone, Lifeline, Residential Wireless, and AT&T Partner exchange.
The general consumer AT&T refer-a-friend program (prepaid, historically $25–$75) is a different, older mechanism and was not verified here.

steps.text: As an existing AT&T wireless or FirstNet Subscriber Paid customer, request your referral link (or QR code) from the Refer-a-Friend portal.
Give the link to a prospective new customer who is eligible for FirstNet service (public-safety employee/volunteer, or supporting entity).
The new customer verifies FirstNet eligibility within 30 days, orders a new line on an eligible FirstNet unlimited plan (minimum $54/month), and activates the Referral Offer.
Keep the new line active for 30 days; AT&T sends reward notification within 60 days of eligible activation — redeem within 75 days; the $100 Visa Reward Card arrives 3–4 weeks after redemption.
steps.done_when: The account stays open and in good standing.

what: the state will match the first $600 that you contribute to your Quest529 account during 2026. You must contribute at least $100 during 2026 to be eligible.
reward: the state will match the first $600 that you contribute to your Quest529 account during 2026. You must contribute at least $100 during 2026 to be eligible.
requirements: Quest529 account owner who is a Kansas resident, not a minor or someone else's tax dependent, with 2025 household federal AGI greater than $0 and at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.
payout_timing: 2026 program year: application due December 1, 2026; qualifying contributions during calendar 2026; match deposited by January 31, 2027.
payout_value_note: Dollar-for-dollar match on own 2026 contributions of $100-$600.
catches: Kansas residents only; 2025 household federal AGI must be above $0 and at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (e.g., $66,000 for a 4-person household).
Dollar-for-dollar on YOUR contributions: contribute $100, get $100; contribute $600, get $600; contribute $0, get $0.
Capped at 1,000 participants statewide (250 per congressional district), first-come, first-served - applying does not guarantee a slot.
Any withdrawal from the account during 2026 disqualifies that beneficiary for the 2026 match.
Rollovers from other 529 plans are not match-eligible.

Matching funds must be used for the beneficiary's qualified education expenses; a non-qualified withdrawal must be repaid to the State of Kansas and faces federal/state taxes plus possible federal penalties - consult a tax advisor.

steps.text: Open a Quest529 account at Quest529.com if you do not already have one.
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Complete the 2026 KIDS Program Application.
Attach 2025 federal tax returns or IRS transcripts for all household members required to file.
Mail the application and documents so they are received by the Kansas State Treasurer's Office no later than December 1, 2026 (supporting documents within 14 days of application).
steps.done_when: It's in the mail to you.

steps.text: Contribute $100-$600 to the KIDS Contribution Account during calendar 2026.
The matching grant is deposited to the Match Account no later than January 31, 2027.

requirements: Maryland resident account owner 18+; Maryland resident beneficiary under 26 in the prior calendar year; AGI within the published bands (individual ≤$112,500 / joint ≤$175,000); account opened after 12/31/2016; minimum contribution by Nov 1; application by May 31; prior state contributions under $9,000.
payout_timing: Annual program: application by May 31; minimum contribution by November 1 of the application year.
payout_value_note: state contribution of $250 or $500 by income band, per the official Maryland529 table
catches: Savings, not income: the state contribution goes into the 529 account — it is a boost to planned college savings, not spendable cash.

Income-banded: individual AGI $49,999 or less (joint $74,999 or less) contributing $25+ gets $500; individual $50,000–$87,499 (joint $75,000–$124,999) contributing $100+ gets $500; individual $87,500–$112,500 (joint $125,000–$175,000) contributing $250+ gets $250. Over the cap = ineligible.
Receiving a state contribution in a year forfeits the Maryland income subtraction (up to $2,500/year/beneficiary) on your own contributions that year — the net benefit is smaller than the headline.
Application deadline: 11:59 pm ET May 31; the minimum contribution must be made by 11:59 pm ET November 1 of the application year. Miss either and you get nothing.
Beneficiary must be a Maryland resident under age 26 in the calendar year before application; account must have been opened after December 31, 2016.
One application per account owner/beneficiary relationship; a beneficiary may receive only two state contributions in any year; prior $9,000 in state contributions = ineligible.
Subject to changes by the Maryland General Assembly — the legislature can alter or end the program.
Standard 529 tax risk: non-qualified withdrawals face federal income tax plus a 10% federal penalty on earnings (and Maryland may recapture deductions) — consult a tax professional.

steps.text: Open a Maryland College Investment Plan 529 account if you don't have one (must be an account opened after December 31, 2016).
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Check your AGI against the official table to find your band and minimum contribution ($25 for $500, $100 for $500, or $250 for $250).
Submit the Save4College State Contribution Program application by 11:59 pm ET on May 31.
Make at least the band's minimum contribution to the applied-for account by 11:59 pm ET on November 1 of the application year.

what: eligible to receive the $100 CollegeBoundbaby Grant
reward: eligible to receive the $100 CollegeBoundbaby Grant
requirements: Children born to or adopted by Rhode Island families, enrolled before the child's first birthday or within one year of adoption.
payout_timing: One-time: enroll within one year of birth or adoption; the $100 grant is deposited to the CollegeBound account.
payout_value_note: Flat $100 state grant per eligible child; no contribution required.
catches: Rhode Island birth or adoption only, and enrollment must happen before the child's first birthday or within the first year of adoption - miss the window and there is no grant.
The grant, including any earnings on it, cannot be transferred to another child, withdrawn for a non-education purpose, or moved to another 529 plan.
Grant funds are disbursed directly to the eligible college or trade/vocational school, not to you.
Non-qualified withdrawals face federal income tax on earnings plus a 10% federal penalty - consult a tax advisor.

steps.text: Check the CollegeBoundbaby box on the hospital birth worksheet, OR self-enroll by submitting the CollegeBoundbaby Authorization Form within one year of the child's birth or adoption.
The $100 grant is deposited into the child's CollegeBound account.
When the child enrolls in college, funds are disbursed by the RI Treasurer directly to the eligible school.

what: The match is up to the first $500 contributed to the account of the current Program year. Yes, we will match dollar for dollar up to the $500.
reward: The match is up to the first $500 contributed to the account of the current Program year. Yes, we will match dollar for dollar up to the $500.
requirements: Colorado resident parent/guardian who can claim the beneficiary as a dependent; family AGI at/below the program-year income chart; beneficiary 8 or younger at initial application (18 max in later years); CollegeInvest 529 account open at application time; one application per beneficiary per year; up to 5 awards per beneficiary.
payout_timing: Annual program: apply typically October–December; contribute during the program year; award paid in the first quarter following the program year; up to 5 annual awards per beneficiary.
payout_value_note: dollar-for-dollar match on account-owner contributions, capped at $500 per program year (official terms)
catches: Dollar-for-dollar match on your own contributions: contribute $350, get $350; contribute $0, get $0. It is a savings boost on planned college savings, not free money.
Subject to availability of funds — eligibility confirmation does not guarantee the award.
Must apply during the annual application period (typically October through December) and REAPPLY every year with fresh federal tax forms; no application, no award.
Income-eligible only: family AGI at or below the program-year income chart; chart updates yearly.
Beneficiary must be 8 years old or younger at the time of the initial application (up to 18 in later years); account must already be open at application time.
Only account-owner contributions qualify — Upromise, Ugift, employer promotions, and other third-party contributions do not.
Award goes into a separate CollegeInvest-owned account and can only be disbursed directly to institutions of higher education (tuition/fees) — not to you.
Use-it-or-lose-it: funds must start being used within 4 years of age of maturity (typically 18) and be fully used within 6 years, or they are revoked.
Standard 529 tax risk: earnings withdrawn for non-qualified expenses face federal income tax plus a 10% federal penalty (and possible state tax consequences) — consult a tax professional.

steps.text: Open a CollegeInvest 529 Savings account with yourself as owner and your child (8 or younger at first application) as beneficiary.
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: During the annual application period (typically October–December), submit the Matching Grant application with your CollegeInvest account number and PDFs of federal tax forms for all parents/guardians in the household.
Contribute to the account during the program year (typically the calendar year) — up to $500 of account-owner contributions to earn the full $500 match.

The matching award is deposited into a CollegeInvest-owned account for your child in the first quarter after the program year ends; it can only be disbursed directly to an institution of higher education.

what: If qualified, we will match your contributions dollar-for-dollar up to $300 per year for five years for a maximum of $1,500 per beneficiary.
reward: If qualified, we will match your contributions dollar-for-dollar up to $300 per year for five years for a maximum of $1,500 per beneficiary.
requirements: Nevada resident account owner and Nevada resident beneficiary; existing Future Path 529 account; beneficiary 13 or younger as of Dec 31 of the first application year; household income $74,999 or less; apply/reapply each year between April 1 and July 31.
payout_timing: Annual cycle: apply April 1–July 31; contributions during the calendar year; match deposited the following January; up to 5 years / $1,500 lifetime per beneficiary.
payout_value_note: dollar-for-dollar match up to $300 per year, lifetime max $1,500 per beneficiary over five years (official terms)
catches: Dollar-for-dollar match on your own contributions: save $100, get $100; save $300+, get the full $300. It is a savings boost on planned college savings, not free money.
First-come, first-served and subject to availability of funds — there is 'no guarantee of the continued operation' of the program; qualifying and applying does not guarantee an award.
You must APPLY or RE-APPLY every year inside your Future Path 529 account — the link opens April 1 and closes July 31; miss the window and that year's match is gone.
Residency + income + age gates: both owner and beneficiary must be Nevada residents, household income $74,999 or less, beneficiary age 13 or younger as of Dec 31 of the first application year.
You must already have a Future Path 529 account — the grant cannot be the reason to open one from scratch (it can, actually, but the account must exist at application).
Matching funds are deposited the following January — roughly a year after you start saving for that year's match.
Lifetime maximum $1,500 per beneficiary over five years — one application per beneficiary per year.
Standard 529 tax risk: non-qualified withdrawals face federal income tax plus a 10% federal penalty on earnings (and possible state tax consequences) — consult a tax professional.

steps.text: Open or keep a Future Path 529 Plan account with a beneficiary age 13 or younger (as of Dec 31 of the first application year).
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Between April 1 and July 31, log into FuturePath529.com, open the beneficiary's account, and click 'Apply / Re-Apply for the Silver State Matching Grant' — repeat every year.
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Save during the calendar year (January 1–December 31) — up to $300 of your contributions earns the full $300 match.
The matching grant is deposited into the beneficiary's account the following January.

what: allows North Dakota residents who have opened a College SAVE Account to be considered for a BND Match in an amount up to $300.00. The BND Match amount is a dollar-for-dollar match and is based on contributions up to $300.00 made to a College SAVE Account by a North Dakota resident who meets eligibil
reward: allows North Dakota residents who have opened a College SAVE Account to be considered for a BND Match in an amount up to $300.00. The BND Match amount is a dollar-for-dollar match and is based on contributions up to $300.00 made to a College SAVE Account by a North Dakota resident who meets eligibility requirements according to their federally adjusted gross income.
requirements: North Dakota resident who recently filed a ND state income tax return as a resident; federally adjusted gross income $0–$100,000 (single) or $0–$150,000 (married filing jointly); beneficiary age 15 or younger; apply within 12 months of opening a College SAVE account; one BND Match per beneficiary.
payout_timing: Apply within 12 months of account opening; contributions within the same 12-month window earn the match; one match per beneficiary.
payout_value_note: dollar-for-dollar match on contributions within 12 months of opening, capped at $300 per beneficiary (official terms)
catches: Dollar-for-dollar match on your own contributions: contribute $300 within 12 months of opening to get the full $300. Savings boost on planned college savings, not free money.
Funding-dependent: Bank of North Dakota can reduce, modify, or stop the match at any time — applying does not guarantee an award.
You must apply within 12 months of opening the College SAVE account (opt in during online enrollment or file the paper BND Match Application); one match per designated beneficiary.
Income gates: federally adjusted gross income $0–$100,000 single or $0–$150,000 married filing jointly, verified via your North Dakota state income tax return (recent ND filer required).
Residency gate: participant must be a North Dakota resident who recently filed a ND state income tax return as a resident.
Beneficiary must not yet have turned 16 (15 or younger).
Match funds live in a BND-owned Match Account and may only be paid directly to the Eligible Educational Institution for qualified education expenses — never paid to you.

Forfeiture risk: rollovers to another state's 529, certain beneficiary changes, account closure without using the match within 18 months, or misrepresentation can fully or partially forfeit the match and earnings.
Standard 529 tax risk: while the program is designed so qualified-use matches aren't taxed, the form notes the IRS could take a different position — consult a tax advisor.

steps.text: Open a North Dakota College SAVE 529 account with a beneficiary age 15 or younger.
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Opt in to the BND Match during online enrollment, or complete and submit the paper BND Match Application (with required tax records) within 12 months of opening the account.
Contribute to the account within the first 12 months after opening — up to $300 of contributions earns the full $300 match.

If approved, the match is deposited into a BND-owned Match Account (within ~60 days of application approval); request a qualified withdrawal to pay the beneficiary's eligible school directly when the time comes.

what: $100 Initial Matching Grant. Open your account, add $25 and get a $100 Initial Matching Grant.
reward: $100 Initial Matching Grant. Open your account, add $25 and get a $100 Initial Matching Grant.
requirements: Maine resident account owner OR Maine resident beneficiary; open a NextGen 529 account and contribute $25; one Initial Matching Grant per beneficiary. (Babies eligible for the separate $500 Alfond Grant have different rules.)
payout_timing: One-time grant awarded automatically after the qualifying $25 contribution; ongoing program with no stated end date.
payout_value_note: flat $100 grant for a $25 contribution to a new NextGen 529 account (official terms)
catches: Savings, not income: the $100 Initial Matching Grant is paid into the NextGen 529 account and can only be paid directly to an eligible institution of higher education — never to you.
Grant funds (including earnings) remain the property of FAME until paid directly to the school, and cannot be transferred to another beneficiary.
Grants are invested at FAME's discretion in a Matching Grant Portfolio and may lose value — the $100 headline can fluctuate.
Eligibility: either the account owner or the beneficiary must be a Maine resident; one grant per beneficiary.
You must open the account AND make the $25 contribution — the grant is awarded automatically after the qualifying contribution, not at account opening alone.

The separate $500 Alfond Grant, $100 Financial Wellness Grant, $100 Automated Funding Grant, and 30% NextStep Matching Grant are DIFFERENT mechanisms — this route covers only the $100 Initial Matching Grant.
See the Terms and Conditions of Maine Grant Programs for other conditions and restrictions.
Standard 529 tax risk: non-qualified withdrawals face federal income tax plus a 10% federal penalty on earnings (and possible state tax consequences) — consult a tax professional.

steps.text: Open a NextGen 529 account (Connect, Direct, or via an advisor for Select) with yourself as owner and/or your child as beneficiary — at least one of you must be a Maine resident.
steps.done_when: The account is open in your name.

steps.text: Contribute at least $25 to the account.

FAME awards the $100 Initial Matching Grant automatically after the qualifying contribution and notifies you by letter or email; the grant appears on your account statement but remains FAME property until paid to a school.

what: Get an $80 Amazon Gift Card upon approval. Terms and conditions apply.
reward: Get an $80 Amazon Gift Card upon approval. Terms and conditions apply.
requirements: New Amazon Store Card applicants with an Amazon.com account; subject to Synchrony Bank credit approval. Existing cardholders are not eligible.
payout_timing: One-time bonus on approval; limited-time offer with no stated end date — the amount ($80 today) can change.
payout_value_note: Amazon Gift Card (store credit) loaded to the amazon.com account on approval; not cash, usable only for Amazon purchases
catches: Gift card, not income or cash: the $80 loads to your Amazon.com account as store credit usable only for Amazon purchases.
LIMITED-TIME offer and subject to credit approval — if you are not approved, there is no bonus (you may instead be considered for the Amazon Secured Card, which requires a security deposit).
Never open or use the card for spending you would not already do: the bonus is on approval, not on purchases.
No annual fee per the official page, but the Store Card variable purchase APR is 29.99% (per the official Synchrony terms) — carrying any balance wipes out the $80 gift card fast.
Full application = hard inquiry on your credit report; late fee up to $40 on Store Card features.

steps.text: Apply for the Amazon Store Card on amazon.com (requires an Amazon.com account) and receive Synchrony Bank credit approval.
On approval, the $80 Amazon Gift Card is automatically and instantly loaded into your Amazon wallet.
Use the gift-card balance toward a future Amazon purchase you already planned.
Pay any card balance in full by the due date so the 29.99% APR never applies.
steps.done_when: The balance is paid in full.
